html:
The capital of South Korea, on the Han River in the west of the Korean peninsula, and capital of Korean states for over six hundred years.

The kingdom of Baekje had its first capital in the area until 475. In 1394 the founder of Joseon made the town of Hanyang his capital and ringed it with walls. The palace of Gyeongbokgung was built the next year. Seoul stayed the royal seat until the end of the dynasty.

Under Japanese rule from 1910 to 1945 the city was called Keijō, and it grew into a modern colonial capital. On 1 March 1919 a reading of a declaration of independence in Seoul started the March 1st Movement, which spread across Korea.

In the Korean War the city changed hands four times and was left in ruins. From the 1960s it became the engine of South Korea's fast growth, linked to Busan by the Gyeongbu Expressway and later to the world by Incheon Airport. About half of all South Koreans now live in the Seoul region. It is home to one of the world's largest churches, Yoido Full Gospel Church, and its wealthy Gangnam district gave its name to the 2012 hit Gangnam Style.
sum: The capital of South Korea, on the Han River in the west of the Korean peninsula, and capital of Korean states for over six hundred years.
